note: Colouring 1 turns the muted olive dark marks in the orange foliage into a solid, cell-edged black blob, while colouring 2 keeps a plain red/yellow foliage dither that loses the marks but reads more naturally.

Colouring 2 puts a sparse patch of red dots into the black/white-dotted bark where colouring 1 keeps grey-white dots; the brown bark is matched by neither and the difference is barely visible at normal distance.
Colouring 1 renders the silver belt/buckle area as white dots on black that read as grey, while colouring 2 fills it with more black and stray red, losing the belt.
